section_summary: This section documents the worldwide transfer, examination, storage, and financial administration of former Japanese diplomatic and consular archives and property after the war. Major files concern Japanese records in Beirut, Cairo, Havana, Mexico City, Bogotá, Santiago, Panama, Rome, and Vatican City, including inventories, intelligence assessments, inter-Allied custody agreements, trust accounts, and proposed sales of furniture. The surviving records were generally judged fragmentary or of limited intelligence value, although the Beirut files contained studies by Takashi Hayashi and a visa blacklist, while Havana’s records identified several potentially noteworthy Japanese residents.

subfiles.title: Department telegram on Japanese official and private property
subfiles.to: American diplomatic representative at Vatican City, Rome
subfiles.about: Instructions governing storage, sale, and financial administration of former Japanese diplomatic property.
subfiles.summary: State sees no objection to the proposed procedure, favors storing Japanese official property unless costly, and puts official and private funds and sale proceeds into a joint Allied trust account, with withdrawals for custody and limited indigent relief.

subfiles.title: Airgram reporting no Japanese mission in Honduras
subfiles.about: Honduras reports that it cannot supply the requested Japanese-property report because no Japanese diplomatic mission existed there.
subfiles.summary: Honduras airgram: there was never a Japanese diplomatic mission there, so the requested property reports can't be made.

subfiles.title: Fragmentary San José report on Japanese property
subfiles.about: A badly degraded Embassy record concerning former Japanese diplomatic property in Costa Rica.
subfiles.summary: Fragmentary San Jose embassy report mentioning Japanese property; most text lost, apparently a reply to the Department's property inquiry.

subfiles.title: Referral of British aide-mémoire on access to archives in Japan
subfiles.about: Referral of a British request concerning access to records and archives in Japan.
subfiles.summary: Memorandum cites a regulation centralizing German, Italian-Fascist and Japanese archives in FC and forwards the British Embassy's October 12, 1945 aide-memoire on British access to Japanese records, pending since November.

subfiles.title: Despatch No. 1085: Documents in Japanese Language Discovered in Files of Former Japanese Consulate in Beirut
subfiles.from: Gordon H. Mattison, U.S. Legation, Beirut
subfiles.about: Transmission of Alfred Regensburger’s examination of Japanese-language records from the former Beirut consulate.
subfiles.summary: Mattison reports Japanese-language expert Alfred Regensburger examined Beirut consulate material January 7-9 and found nothing of particular interest; records were repacked and stored, and the Japanese books might go to the Legation library or the Library of Congress.

subfiles.title: Report of Japanese Translator on Records of Beirut Jap Consulate
subfiles.about: Detailed assessment of the surviving Japanese consular correspondence, Takashi Hayashi’s papers, and a visa blacklist.
subfiles.summary: Regensburger finds nearly all sensitive wartime records destroyed or removed, leaving routine trade, cultural and propaganda files; Takashi Hayashi's papers include Egypt studies and a Middle East diary, meetings with Riad Solh and Adil Arslan, and a 1937 thirty-seven-entry visa blacklist.

subfiles.title: Handwritten routing notes on the Beirut records
subfiles.about: Brief internal notes asking that the Beirut material be retained temporarily and recording a promised callback.
subfiles.summary: One note asks 'Joe' to keep the material for a while in connection with Japanese work. A second says that Simpson will call back; the remaining handwriting is largely illegible.

subfiles.title: Airgram A-29 on continued storage of Beirut consular property
subfiles.about: Instructions for storing or selling former Japanese consular property and controlling access to Japanese books.
subfiles.summary: Airgram A-29: keep Beirut consular property stored, selling non-archival movables only if deteriorating or too costly, proceeds to a joint Allied trust account; Japanese books stay nominally Japanese but may be stored for Allied mission use.

subfiles.title: Despatch No. 1279: Relinquishment by the Swiss Government of Japanese Archives and Property in Egypt
subfiles.from: S. Pinkney Tuck, American Legation, Cairo
subfiles.about: Report on the Swiss transfer of Japanese official archives and property to the Four Powers and then to Egyptian guardianship.
subfiles.summary: Despatch 1279: the Swiss delivered Japanese archives, furniture and personal property in Egypt to the Chinese, Soviet, British and U.S. representatives, who placed it under provisional Egyptian guardianship (Mohamed Aly Sadek Bey) retaining disposition authority; furniture to be sold, sealed archives examined and kept.

subfiles.title: Procès-verbal concerning Japanese official premises, furniture, and archives in Egypt
subfiles.from: Alfred Brunner, Swiss minister in Egypt
subfiles.to: B. C. Flynn, C. B. Lyon, P. M. Dneprov, and Chang Chi-Hsien
subfiles.about: Formal transfer of the former Japanese Legation and consular furniture and archives to the Allied representatives.
subfiles.summary: Brunner places the Japanese government’s furniture and archives at Cairo in the custody of the British, American, Soviet, and Chinese representatives. The instrument incorporates inventories for the Cairo Legation and the consulates at Alexandria and Port Said and records removal of the Swiss protective plaque.

subfiles.title: Procès-verbal concerning private property of Japanese diplomatic and consular agents
subfiles.from: Alfred Brunner, Swiss minister in Egypt
subfiles.to: Representatives of the United Kingdom, United States, Soviet Union, and China
subfiles.about: Formal transfer of private property belonging to former Japanese diplomatic and consular personnel.
subfiles.summary: The Swiss minister consigns to the four Allied representatives private property belonging to Japanese diplomatic and consular agents and held in the former Cairo Legation. The parties certify that the previously supplied inventory had been checked and found accurate.

subfiles.title: Procès-verbal concerning private property of Japanese nationals
subfiles.from: Alfred Brunner, Swiss minister in Egypt
subfiles.to: Representatives of the United Kingdom, United States, Soviet Union, and China
subfiles.about: Formal transfer of private property belonging to Japanese civilians in Egypt.
subfiles.summary: Brunner transfers private property of Japanese nationals stored at the former Cairo Legation to the four Allied representatives. The instrument notes an attached recapitulatory valuation of the various sequestrated Japanese goods and confirms the prior inventory.

subfiles.title: Record of transfer to provisional Egyptian control and guardianship
subfiles.from: Representatives of China, the Soviet Union, the United Kingdom, and the United States
subfiles.to: Mohamed Aly Sadek Bey for the Egyptian Government
subfiles.about: Placement of Japanese archives and property under temporary Egyptian guardianship on behalf of the Four Powers.
subfiles.summary: Record of delivery of the former Japanese Legation's archives and property to Mohamed Aly Sadek Bey at Zamalek, for provisional Egyptian control in the Four Powers' name, subject to their revision, per the January 16 Swiss inventory.

subfiles.title: Despatch No. 925 transmitting report on Japanese Legation archives in Havana
subfiles.from: H. Bartlett Wells, U.S. Embassy, Havana
subfiles.about: Covering despatch for an Embassy report on the Japanese archives and property held in Havana.
subfiles.summary: Wells answers the November 1945 circular, forwarding a report on the Havana takeover of Japanese records and property, with copies to the military, naval and legal attachés.

subfiles.title: Report on Japanese Legation Archives and Property in Havana
subfiles.about: Assessment of Japanese registration cards, letters, maps, and office property held by the Cuban Ministry of State.
subfiles.summary: Cuba's Ministry of State held sealed boxes of furniture and insignificant papers and a Japanese residents' card file, examined for notable people such as Naoji Iwaki and Kiyoshi Uchiyama; three letters and two maps were of little value, so the Embassy found the collection almost negligible.

subfiles.title: Contents of Safe
subfiles.about: Inventory of Japanese-language books, stamps, correspondence, press files, diplomatic telegrams, and other objects found in a safe associated with Iraq.
subfiles.summary: Safe contents list: Japanese ledgers, stamps, seals, press and radio files, telegrams, payroll, publications, and files on Iraqi affairs, the Rashid Ali rebellion and petroleum.

subfiles.title: Letter to the British ambassador on Japanese funds in Chile
subfiles.from: Hugh Millard for the U.S. ambassador
subfiles.to: John Hurleston Leche, British ambassador in Chile
subfiles.about: Proposal to retain the existing Chilean arrangement for Japanese funds and Swedish protective expenditures.
subfiles.summary: Millard tells the British ambassador the main Japanese funds are held in trust for the Four Powers and 304,544.18 Chilean pesos were left with the Swedish Legation for routine protection, so no additional access to the trust account should be arranged.

subfiles.title: Telegram No. 113 reporting the Cairo transfer
subfiles.about: Notice that the Swiss representative had transferred Japanese archives and property to the Four Powers, which placed them with the Egyptian Foreign Office.
subfiles.summary: Tuck reports completion of the Swiss transfer and the subsequent delivery of custody to the Egyptian Foreign Office. He states that a despatch will follow. Pages 560-561 contain largely illegible handwritten routing or follow-up notes associated with the telegram.

subfiles.title: Despatch No. 27,994: Disposal of Japanese Archives
subfiles.from: Raymond H. Geist for the U.S. ambassador, Mexico City
subfiles.about: Urgent request for instructions on disposition of Japanese archives held by the Swedish Legation in Mexico.
subfiles.summary: Geist: the Soviet Embassy presses for decisions on Japanese archives, funds and property while British instructions suggest sending archives to Washington; State gave guidance on funds and property but not archives, so he asks urgently as the British, Chinese and Soviets are ready to act.

subfiles.title: Memorandum of conversation with Grigori Kasparov
subfiles.about: Discussion of Soviet proposals for Japanese assets, archives, rent, and payments to the Japanese Committee in Mexico.
subfiles.summary: Kasparov says Moscow favors dividing all Japanese assets among the Four Powers and wants Soviet study of archives, objecting to 8,300 pesos monthly to a Japanese Committee and continued rent; Geist says the ambassador awaits Department instructions.

subfiles.title: Despatch No. 625 transmitting Item No. 86 of the Panama archives inventory
subfiles.from: V. Lansing Collins Jr. for the U.S. ambassador, Panama
subfiles.about: Transmission of a carbon copy of a Japanese-language archival item requested by the Department.
subfiles.summary: Collins sends one of five carbon copies of Item 86 from the surviving Japanese archives inventory in Panama, per the January 14 request; it need not be returned.

subfiles.title: Copy of Item No. 86 from the Japanese archives in Panama
subfiles.about: A short Japanese or Chinese-character document preserved as Item No. 86 of the Panama inventory.
subfiles.summary: Copy of Item 86 from the Japanese archives in Panama, mostly East Asian characters; contents can't be reliably read.

subfiles.title: Airgram A-33 reporting no Japanese funds in Ciudad Trujillo
subfiles.about: Report that no Japanese cash or liquid resources existed locally and that no action was required.
subfiles.summary: Airgram A-33: Ciudad Trujillo reports no Japanese cash or liquid funds, so no action is being taken.

subfiles.title: Memorandum on Japanese documents captured in Rome
subfiles.from: Wade H. Coleman Jr., Office of Naval Intelligence
subfiles.to: Frederick B. Lyon, Department of State
subfiles.about: Offer to transfer Japanese documents captured at Mitsubishi Shoji Kaisha premises in Rome before their disposal.
subfiles.summary: Naval Intelligence holds Japanese documents captured after Rome's fall, mostly from Mitsubishi Shoji premises and possibly relevant to Safehaven; since the Navy no longer needs them, Coleman asks whether State wants them before disposal.

subfiles.title: State Department request for captured Rome documents
subfiles.from: Frederick B. Lyon, Department of State
subfiles.to: Wade H. Coleman Jr., Navy Department
subfiles.about: Request that the Navy provide State with the Japanese documents captured in Rome and any available index or summary.
subfiles.summary: Lyon accepts the Navy's offer, asks that the captured Rome documents be sent to State for review, and requests any Navy index or summary.

subfiles.title: Telegram from Vatican City requesting expedited reply
subfiles.about: Request for an expedited response to an earlier Vatican City telegram.
subfiles.summary: Gowen says he has been asked to expedite a reply to AMVAT telegram 241 of December 19.

subfiles.title: Messersmith letter seeking instructions on Mexican Japanese assets
subfiles.about: Private request for clear authority to negotiate with British, Soviet, and Chinese colleagues over Japanese archives and funds in Mexico.
subfiles.summary: Messersmith opposes the Soviet proposal to divide Japanese assets, favors keeping funds under the four chiefs of mission, agrees the 8,300-peso monthly payment needs review, and asks Carrigan to hasten instructions with specific limits or broad discretion.

subfiles.title: Department telegram rejecting division of Japanese funds in Mexico
subfiles.about: Department approval of Messersmith’s opposition to dividing Japanese funds and notice of a planned expert archival mission.
subfiles.summary: State agrees Japanese funds and proceeds shouldn't be divided and its circular won't change, supports cutting Japanese Committee payments to the minimum, and expects an expert team to examine the Mexico City archives.

subfiles.title: Messersmith follow-up letter on Despatch No. 27,994
subfiles.about: Request that Messersmith’s fuller personal letter be considered with the formal despatch on Japanese archives.
subfiles.summary: Messersmith says Despatch 27,994 was incomplete, asks Carrigan to put his personal letter before responsible officers, and needs specific directives or full latitude with his three Allied colleagues.

subfiles.title: Carrigan acknowledgment to Messersmith
subfiles.about: Acknowledgment that Messersmith’s letter was added to the file and shown to the responsible officers.
subfiles.summary: Carrigan acknowledges Messersmith's January 23 request, says his earlier letter reached the archives officers, and hopes the new circular airgram helps.

subfiles.title: Despatch No. 334: Possession Taken of Japanese Archives and Property in Colombia
subfiles.from: John C. Wiley, U.S. Embassy, Bogotá
subfiles.about: Report on Allied acquisition, storage, and proposed disposal of Japanese archives, funds, furniture, and private property in Colombia.
subfiles.summary: Wiley: after Switzerland ended protecting Japan, its chargé surrendered archives, property and funds to the American, British and Soviet missions; archives sealed at the British residence, 82,438.42 pesos await unfreezing, and a discreet auction of ordinary furniture and a car is planned, preserving archives, pictures and vases.

subfiles.title: Wiley note requesting Swiss transfer of Japanese assets
subfiles.about: Four-Power request for the transfer of Japanese archives, property, and funds to joint Allied custody in Colombia.
subfiles.summary: Wiley asks that Japanese archives, property and funds at the Swiss Legation go to the American, British and Soviet missions pending a Chinese representative, and that Switzerland keep protecting Japanese nationals if convenient.

subfiles.title: Rossat reply agreeing to transfer Japanese assets
subfiles.about: Swiss acceptance of the requested inspection and transfer of former Japanese archives, property, and funds.
subfiles.summary: Rossat says Swiss instructions allow compliance, with inspection December 22 and transfer December 27; he'll consult Bern on continuing protection of Japanese nationals.

subfiles.title: Memorandum on Allied planning for the Bogotá transfer
subfiles.about: Record of American, British, and Soviet planning for custody and disposal of Japanese assets and archives.
subfiles.summary: Participants agree Wiley will request the Swiss transfer and a three-mission committee will manage archives, furniture and personal-property cases; they discuss discreet furniture sales, landlord claims, preserving Japanese prints and Soviet language expertise; Wiley will press to unblock funds.

subfiles.title: Wiley memorandum of conversation with the Swiss chargé
subfiles.about: Discussion of the impending Japanese-asset transfer, safes, private property, and possible missing personal archives.
subfiles.summary: Swiss chargé welcomes the Four-Power transfer and describes the Legation building and safes; Wiley suggests leaving built-in safes with the landlord and selling a Japanese merchant's car into a blocked account; the former minister's archives may be with the gardener.

subfiles.title: Letter establishing joint account for Japanese funds
subfiles.from: Gerald A. Mokma for the U.S. ambassador
subfiles.to: National City Bank of New York, Bogotá
subfiles.about: Instructions for depositing 82,438.42 Colombian pesos under three-mission joint control.
subfiles.summary: Mokma deposits the former Japanese funds in an account jointly held by the British Embassy, Soviet Legation and U.S. Embassy; each mission's authorized signature is needed for withdrawal.

subfiles.title: Snow letter on storage and transfer arrangements
subfiles.about: British confirmation of arrangements for transferring and storing Japanese archives and personal effects in Bogotá.
subfiles.summary: Snow encloses his letter to Colombia's foreign minister, records the plan for the senior Allied representative to receive Japanese archives, property and funds from Rossat, and offers Chapinero storage for the archives and five cases of the former minister's effects.

subfiles.title: Snow letter requesting unblocking of Japanese funds
subfiles.about: Request for Colombian action to unblock Japanese funds when the Swiss protecting power releases them.
subfiles.summary: Snow tells Colombia's foreign minister Switzerland will transfer Japanese archives, property and funds to the American, Soviet and British missions, asks prompt unblocking of funds, and promises money for protecting Japanese nationals remains available.

subfiles.title: Swiss note ending protection of Japanese interests in Colombia
subfiles.about: Notification that Switzerland will not continue protecting Japanese interests or nationals in Colombia.
subfiles.summary: Rossat says Switzerland declined to continue protecting Japanese interests in Colombia and transfers the archives, property and funds already taken by the Allied missions plus full responsibility for Japanese interests.

subfiles.title: Procès-verbal of the transfer of Japanese archives, property, and funds in Bogotá
subfiles.to: Gerald A. Mokma, Frank Collinge Ogden, and Simeon A. Gonionskii
subfiles.about: Formal record of Switzerland’s transfer of all Japanese assets in its custody to the American, British, and Soviet missions.
subfiles.summary: Rossat delivers archives, household contents, an 82,438.42-peso check, safe keys, emblem and flag, five personal-property cases and other Japanese nationals' property; archives couldn't be verified, being sealed, labeled in kanji and received from the Spanish Legation without Swiss responsibility.

subfiles.title: Inventory of Japanese Government furniture and effects in Bogotá
subfiles.to: American and British Embassies and Soviet Legation
subfiles.about: Room-by-room inventory of furniture, fixtures, office equipment, and household effects in the former Japanese Legation.
subfiles.summary: The inventory covers reception rooms, bedrooms, offices, archives, dining areas, kitchen, service rooms, and corridors throughout the former Legation. It lists furniture, carpets, curtains, safes, filing cabinets, artwork, a piano, radiola, ping-pong table, and Japanese fencing equipment. Several kitchen items remained in the charge of Tomás Tada.

subfiles.title: Archives of Japanese Legation
subfiles.about: Brief box-level description of the sealed archives of the former Japanese Legation in Bogotá.
subfiles.summary: List of six sealed boxes of numbered files, books, clippings, twenty-four film rolls, office equipment and an atlas, bearing American, British and Soviet seals.

subfiles.title: Despatch No. 13,397: Allocation of Japanese funds for protection of Japanese interests in Chile
subfiles.from: Hugh Millard for the U.S. ambassador, Santiago
subfiles.about: Report on the 304,544.18-peso allocation left with the Swedish Legation and the principal Allied trust account.
subfiles.summary: Millard reports principal Japanese cash and liquid resources were taken over in November 1945 for the Four Powers, with 304,544.18 Chilean pesos left with the Swedish Legation for routine protection; the British and Chinese agreed Sweden needs no access to the larger trust account.

subfiles.title: Letter requesting Swedish accounting for Japanese protective funds
subfiles.from: Hugh Millard for the U.S. ambassador
subfiles.to: Tore Högstedt, Swedish chargé d’affaires ad interim
subfiles.about: Request for estimates and expenditure reports covering funds left with Sweden for routine Japanese-interest work.
subfiles.summary: Millard endorses Sweden keeping 304,544.18 pesos, asks how long they'll last, and requests reports for November-December 1945 and January-March 1946, allowing only indigent relief, routine costs and moving or storing property.

subfiles.title: Letter to the Chinese minister on Japanese funds in Chile
subfiles.from: Hugh Millard for the U.S. ambassador
subfiles.to: Chaucer E. Wu, Chinese minister in Chile
subfiles.about: Request for Chinese concurrence in retaining the existing trust-account arrangement for Japanese funds.
subfiles.summary: Millard tells the Chinese minister the main funds are held for the Four Powers and 304,544.18 pesos were left with Sweden, proposing Sweden get no access to the main account unless he objects.

subfiles.title: Duplicate copy of letter to the British ambassador on Japanese funds
subfiles.from: Hugh Millard for the U.S. ambassador
subfiles.to: John Hurleston Leche, British ambassador in Chile
subfiles.about: A heavily degraded duplicate of the proposal to leave Swedish protective funds separate from the Allied trust account.
subfiles.summary: Duplicate of the January 15 letter to the British ambassador explaining the trust account and separate 304,544.18-peso Swedish allocation, proposing no change.

subfiles.title: British Embassy reply approving the Chilean funds arrangement
subfiles.about: British concurrence that Sweden need not access the main Japanese trust account while its separate allocation remains available.
subfiles.summary: Leche calls the Chilean funds arrangement satisfactory, agrees Swedish access and accountability are unnecessary until the money left with Sweden is exhausted, and forwarded copies to the Foreign Office and Washington.

subfiles.title: Chinese Legation reply approving the Chilean funds arrangement
subfiles.from: Tang Wu for the Chinese minister
subfiles.about: Chinese concurrence with the Allied trust account and separate Swedish allocation for protecting Japanese interests.
subfiles.summary: Tang Wu acknowledges the Japanese funds deposited for the Four Powers and agrees the Swedish chargé needs no main-account access since 304,544.18 pesos were left for routine protection.
